The Saint Anselm Crier

Women’s basketball prepares for deep playoff push

Curtis Newton, Crier Staff
February 21, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:12
Instaread

The Saint Anselm Women’s Basketball team is currently 12-8, and are on pace to have a end the season in a very solid position. The team is also 7-8 in the NE10 conference, and are currently in fifth place, tied with Southern New Hampshire University and Saint Michael’s College. The team had a rough start to the NE10 Conference games, suffering four straight losses, but have since started to come back in the standings. Recently, the team suffered a hard loss to the current NE10 frontrunners at Bentley University. Even though the Hawks lost by 10 points, 64-54, there were still many highlights. For example, senior guard Tatum Forbes scored a career-high of 30 points, making up nearly half of Saint Anselm’s total points. This was the first 30-point game by a player on the Hawks since Melanie Hoyt of the class of 2025 scored 31 in 2024 against American International. The Hawks never managed to stay ahead in the game, but they were often within less than ten points of the lead. On February 7th, the team traveled to New York to complete their regular season sweep of Pace University. Senior Forbes once again did extremely well, finishing the game with 21 points, 8 rebounds, and 9 assists. Freshman Hannah Lynch set two career highs, ending the game with 10 points and 8 rebounds, and senior Anna Nelson matched her career high with 8 more rebounds. Pace started the game by hitting three of its first four three-point shots, taking an early lead, but Saint Anselm was able to get ahead in the third quarter, and stayed there for the rest of the game. Saint Anselm returned home to soundly defeat Southern New Hampshire with a score of 77-55. Forbes continued her streak of great performances, finishing with 24 points, and a season high of five steals. Sophomore Bella Vaz was not far behind, though. She reached a career-high of 21 points, with 19 of them being within the first half. She also reached a career-best three-point percentage, knocking down 5 out of 10 shots. While SNHU kept the game within one possession in the first quarter, Saint Anselm quickly ran away with the lead. To honor senior day, the Hawks defeated Franklin Pierce by another massive margin. The game, ending 74-49, saw the class of ‘26, once again led by Tatum Forbes, finish yet another season sweep of an NE10 division rival. Even though Franklin Pierce took a three-point lead in the first quarter, the rest of the game was Saint Anselm all the way. Forbes once again shot over 20 points, followed by senior Nelson with 10 points and 6 assists. All five seniors playing for the Hawks were able to get points this game, leading to a season-high 10 players all shooting baskets. On Wednesday, the Hawks will play the 9-6 Assumption University to hopefully get payback for their most recent 1-point loss, and will then follow that up by traveling to Springfield to play American International and look for another revenge win. The final game of the NE10 regular season will be played on February 24th in Stoutenburgh Gymnasium against Saint Michael’s College.
